{{Short description|House of Representatives of the Philippines legislative district}} {{Use mdy dates|date=February 2021}} {{Infobox constituency | name = Abra's at-large congressional district | parl_name = [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] | image = Abra in Philippines.svg | caption = Location of Abra within the [[Philippines]] | district_label = Province | district = [[Abra (province)|Abra]] | region_label = Region | region = [[Cordillera Administrative Region]] | population = 246,948 (2024){{PH census|2024}} | electorate = 188,957 (2025){{cite web |title=Data on the Total Number Established and Clustered Precincts, Registered Voters and Voting Centers |url=https://comelec.gov.ph/php-tpls-attachments/2025NLE/Statistics/CONSOLIDATED_2025_Number_Of_Registered_Voters.pdf |website=Commission on Elections|accessdate=July 2, 2025}} | area = {{convert|4165.25|sqkm|sqmi|abbr=on}} | year = 1917 (single-member district) | members_label = Representative | members = [[Joseph Bernos]] | blank1_name = Political party | blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}}|border=darkgray}} [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|NUP]] | blank2_name = Congressional bloc | blank2_info = Majority }} '''Abra's at-large congressional district''' refers to the lone [[congressional district of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Abra (province)|Abra]]. Abra has been represented in the country's various [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|national legislatures]] since 1898.{{Cite web |date=1999 |title=The Malolos Congress: A Centennial publication on the inauguration of the Philippine Republic (January 23, 1899 – January 3, 1999) |url=https://archive.org/details/TheMalolosCongress/page/n77/mode/1up |access-date=May 16, 2020 |publisher=[[National Historical Commission of the Philippines]]}} The first congressional delegation consisted of two members in the [[First Philippine Republic]] legislature known as the [[Malolos Congress (1898)|Malolos Congress]]. Since 1917 when it was re-established as a regular province separate from [[Ilocos Sur]], Abra has been entitled to one member in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]], elected provincewide [[at-large]], except for a brief period between 1943 and 1944 when it was again represented by two members in the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly]] of the [[Second Philippine Republic]].{{Cite web |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |access-date=May 16, 2020 |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} From 1978 to 1984, all provinces were converted into multi-seat regional at-large districts for the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] of the [[Fourth Philippine Republic]], with Abra forming part of the twelve-seat [[Ilocos Region's at-large parliamentary district|Region I's at-large district]]. It was restored as a [[single-member district]] in 1984. The district served as an electoral district in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1934|1934 Constitutional Convention]] and in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1971|1971 Constitutional Convention]], with two delegates representing Abra at-large in each.{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/28/15525|chamber=Act|number=4125|date=May 26, 1934|title=An Act to Provide for the Election and Holding of the Constitutional Convention Authorized by the Act of the Congress of the United States of March Twenty-Fourth, Nineteen Hundred and Thirty-Four, Appropriate Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes}}{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/14108|chamber=RA|number=6132|date=August 24, 1970|title=An Act Implementing Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Two as Amended by Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Four of the Congress of the Philippines Calling for a Constitutional Convention, Providing for Proportional Representation Therein and Other Details Relating to the Election of Delegates to and the Holding of the Constitutional Convention, Repealing for the Purpose Republic Act Four Thousand Nine Hundred Fourteen, and for Other Purposes}} The district is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Joseph Bernos]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP).{{Cite web |title=House Members |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |access-date=May 16, 2020 |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]]}} == Recent election results from province-wide races == {| class="wikitable" !
